acceptance.given: An applicable Toolchain Consumer has completed behavioral rollback during an exercised lifecycle.

oracle.expected: Each applicable Consumer executes its re-enable transition through its real repository call surface and reaches the re-enabled state.
forbidden: Simulating re-enable with a schema file, capability descriptor, or old receipt instead of a real call surface.
oracle.observable: Execution assertions in the real Consumer call-surface tests show rollback followed by re-enable through scripts/sc/skill_package_replay.py or scripts/sc/workflow_model_routing.py.

acceptance.then: The applicable Consumer is re-enabled through a real call surface.
acceptance.when: When the Consumer lifecycle is exercised.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Exercise a purported re-enable path backed only by CLI help, schema, capability descriptor, or receipt; Consumer lifecycle assertions must reject it.
Exercise rollback followed by a real Consumer re-enable call that does not restore enabled state; the lifecycle test must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Exercise each applicable Toolchain Consumer's real call surface across behavioral rollback and re-enable, asserting restored enabled state rather than accepting simulated evidence.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback reverts only Consumer lifecycle handling and preserves the existing replay and workflow-routing public interfaces.

slice_hint.state_transition: An applicable Consumer moves from post-behavioral-rollback to re-enabled through its real call surface.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The applicable Consumer tests execute rollback and re-enable through their real Toolchain call surfaces, reach re-enabled state, and reject simulated evidence.

acceptance.given: S10, S22, and S41 declare their production entry points and pytest selectors, while their declared tests have not yet been authored.

oracle.expected: S10, S22, and S41 each execute through exactly their declared production entry points and corresponding declared pytest selector.
forbidden: Substituting a different production entry point or test selector.
Using a non-executing descriptor or documentation command as a verification path.
oracle.observable: The three declared pytest selectors execute assertions binding S10 to scripts/sc/_semantic_gate_all_runtime.py and scripts/sc/skill_package_replay.py, S22 to validate_implementation.py and scripts/sc/skill_package_replay.py, and S41 to scripts/sc/_semantic_gate_all_runtime.py and scripts/sc/skill_package_replay.py.

acceptance.then: S10, S22, and S41 verification runs use their respective declared production entry points and selectors.
acceptance.when: When running the S10, S22, or S41 verification path.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run each declared slice test with a substituted production entry point or selector; its binding assertion must fail.
Attempt to satisfy any S10, S22, or S41 path with documentation or a descriptor command; the path-fidelity assertion must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Author the three declared slice tests to bind S10, S22, and S41 to their source-declared production entry points and exact pytest selectors, rejecting alternate or non-executing paths.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback removes only path-fidelity enforcement and retains the existing production entry-point interfaces and source-declared selectors.

slice_hint.state_transition: S10, S22, and S41 move from declared-but-unevidenced paths to execution through their declared entry points and exact selectors.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All three declared selectors execute their matching production bindings; any alternate entry point, selector, descriptor, or documentation command fails the corresponding path-fidelity assertion.

acceptance.given: The acceptance lifecycle owner is identified and an actor attempts to publish an acceptance-passed result.

oracle.expected: The publication succeeds only when the actor matches the current Acceptance lifecycle owner; after an ownership change, the former owner is rejected.
forbidden: A former Acceptance lifecycle owner publishes acceptance-passed after ownership changes.
oracle.observable: The test result records the resolved current owner, actor identity, ownership transition, and accept/reject outcome for each publication attempt.

acceptance.then: Evaluate the authorization result after each publication attempt.

failure_intents.selector_intent: The authorization assertion is absent, bypassed, or permits publication by a non-current owner.
The test binds publication authorization to a former owner or an actor other than the resolved current Acceptance lifecycle owner.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce current Acceptance lifecycle-owner authorization for acceptance-passed publication, including rejection after ownership changes.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing artifact formats and lifecycle state; rollback only the owner-check implementation and its test.

slice_hint.state_transition: Unauthorized publication attempts remain rejected; authorized publication is recorded as acceptance-passed for the current owner.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The S27 selector reports acceptance only for the current owner and rejects both non-owner and former-owner publication attempts.

acceptance.given: The six materially distinct Matrix Cases and their Stable subject inputs are loaded for replay.

oracle.expected: Every one of the six Matrix Cases executes the same immutable Stable subject and emits attributable evidence without any mutation.
forbidden: Any case omits the Stable subject.
The Stable subject is mutated during execution.
oracle.observable: The replay evidence contains six case records, each with the Stable subject identity, pre/post identity comparison, and execution result.

acceptance.then: Inspect case-level subject identity and mutation markers after matrix execution.
acceptance.when: When the Matrix Case execution matrix runs.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A matrix case executes without the Stable subject or with a changed Stable subject identity.
The evidence lacks attributable records for one or more of the six Matrix Cases.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Replay each of the six Matrix Cases against one immutable Stable subject and record case-attributable identity evidence.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep replay and matrix artifact schemas backward compatible; revert only subject-identity enforcement and related tests if necessary.

slice_hint.state_transition: All six cases transition from unverified Stable-subject execution to verified immutable execution with attributable evidence.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The S7 pytest invocation proves six Stable-subject executions, each identity remains unchanged, and no case is missing evidence.
